# Attribution

<!-- Generated from data/catalog.yaml by app/src/core/attribution.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

The code is MIT-licensed (`LICENSE`); our curated data and documentation are CC BY 4.0 (`LICENSE-DATA.md`).
The app is built from the published datasets and papers below. We regridded, resampled, recoloured and
combined their data; `scripts/` shows exactly how, and `data/catalog.yaml` lists every file used.

## Data and research

### PALEOMAP PaleoDEMs (Scotese & Wright 2018)

- **Used for:** Terrain and bathymetry for the globe (65 Ma slice, 0.1°)
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Paleo-elevation: C. R. Scotese & N. Wright, PALEOMAP Project (CC BY 4.0)
- **Cite:** Scotese, C. R., & Wright, N. M. (2018). PALEOMAP Paleodigital Elevation Models (PaleoDEMS) for the Phanerozoic. PALEOMAP Project. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5460860
- **Source:** <https://zenodo.org/records/5460860>

### PaleoMAP PaleoCoastlines v7 (Kocsis & Scotese 2021)

- **Used for:** Paleo-shorelines and continental margins; the PALEOMAP plate model (rotations + static polygons) for reconstructing points
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Paleo-coastlines: Á. T. Kocsis & C. R. Scotese (CC BY 4.0)
- **Cite:** Kocsis, Á. T., & Scotese, C. R. (2021). Mapping paleocoastlines and continental flooding during the Phanerozoic. Earth-Science Reviews, 213, 103463. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2020.103463 ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7828387
- **Source:** <https://zenodo.org/records/7828387>

### PhanDA HadCM3L model priors, 66 Ma simulation `texyn` (Judd et al. 2024; simulations by BRIDGE)

- **Used for:** Pre-impact climate (annual mean air temperature and precipitation) that colours the land and sets vegetation. Experiment 96 of suite scotese_spinupa is BRIDGE's texyn run (66 Ma, 576 ppm CO2), republished with a licence.
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Climate: E. J. Judd et al., PhanDA HadCM3L model priors (CC BY 4.0); simulations by P. J. Valdes and BRIDGE, University of Bristol
- **Cite:** Judd, E. J., Tierney, J. E., Lunt, D. J., Montañez, I. P., Huber, B. T., Wing, S. L., & Valdes, P. J. (2024). A 485-million-year history of Earth's surface temperature. Science, 385(6715), eadk3705. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adk3705 ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8237751
- **Source:** <https://zenodo.org/records/8237751>

### Global mean surface temperatures for 100 Phanerozoic intervals (Scotese et al. 2021)

- **Used for:** Proxy-adjusted surface-temperature grids (PALEOMAP frame)
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Paleotemperature: C. R. Scotese, H. Song, B. J. W. Mills & D. G. van der Meer (CC BY 4.0)
- **Cite:** Scotese, C. R., Song, H., Mills, B. J. W., & van der Meer, D. G. (2021). Phanerozoic paleotemperatures: The earth's changing climate during the last 540 million years. Earth-Science Reviews, 215, 103503. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2021.103503 ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5718392
- **Source:** <https://zenodo.org/records/5718392>

## Reference datasets and methods

### Paleobathymetry 0–120 Ma (Dutkiewicz et al. 2019)

- **Used for:** Reference only: ocean depth in the Müller plate frame (not PALEOMAP), so it does not line up with our terrain
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Paleobathymetry: A. Dutkiewicz et al. 2019 (CC BY 4.0)
- **Cite:** Dutkiewicz, A., Müller, R. D., Cannon, J., Vaughan, S., & Zahirovic, S. (2019). Sequestration and subduction of deep-sea carbonate in the global ocean since the Early Cretaceous. Geology, 47(1), 91–94. https://doi.org/10.1130/G45424.1
- **Source:** <https://www.earthbyte.org/webdav/ftp/Data_Collections/Dutkiewicz_etal_2019_Geology/>

### iSALE-3D runs for "A steeply-inclined trajectory for the Chicxulub impact" (Collins et al. 2020)

- **Used for:** Crater-formation reference (inputs and plotting scripts only; the 300 MB timesteps are fetched on demand)
- **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
- **Credit:** Crater formation: G. S. Collins et al. 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
- **Cite:** Collins, G. S., Patel, N., Davison, T. M., et al. (2020). A steeply-inclined trajectory for the Chicxulub impact. Nature Communications, 11, 1480. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15269-x ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3667833
- **Source:** <https://zenodo.org/records/3667833>

### Earth Impact Effects Program equations (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005)

- **Used for:** Distance-dependent local effects (ported in scripts/eiep_reference.py and the app)
- **Licence:** Not stated (we use the published method, not the data)
- **Credit:** Impact-effects scaling: G. S. Collins, H. J. Melosh & R. A. Marcus 2005
- **Cite:** Collins, G. S., Melosh, H. J., & Marcus, R. A. (2005). Earth Impact Effects Program: A Web-based computer program for calculating the regional environmental consequences of a meteoroid impact on Earth. Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 40(6), 817–840. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1945-5100.2005.tb00157.x
